analysis.title: GS Materials Nov 2: Copper's 800kt supply cut, what's your disruption allowance
key_insights: October was the worst month for miners. GSXEMINE fell 10%, SXPP 8.5%, CSI300 7.5%, ASX miners (GSXAAUMI) 12%, GDX 12% and uranium 14%. The author says there was no single trigger, only the US midterms over the weekend.

Oil is driving headlines. GIR raised its Dec26 oil forecast to $105 and its 2027 average to $88 (+$8/bbl) to reflect supply risk. Oil moved from $118 to $109 overnight on diplomacy headlines after Friday's expiry.
GS PB reported that all strategies lost money last week.

The author sees China as the drag on resource equities. China copper and gold equities had some of the largest pullbacks, and Zijin's drawdown is singled out. The author argues the sector struggles until China participates, and last year's rally was led daily by China price action.

China's official manufacturing PMI for October was 49.3 against consensus 49.9 and the desk's estimate of 49.5. Output and new orders contracted, and the new export orders sub-index fell to 48.7 from 50.0.
Cochilco cut its copper supply forecast by 330kt in 2026 and 470kt in 2027, about 800kt in total. The previous update was in August.

The author links the cut to a record onshore China copper premium, an expected fall in refined metal production into year end, and impaired supply. Chile's September output fell 15% y/y and Chile's YTD output is down 9% y/y.
Accidents at block-cave mines (El Teniente, Grasberg, Oyu Tolgoi) are cited as a reminder that this mining method is hard to run.

Many traders see copper tariffs as a post-midterms event. The author questions whether the White House wants US stocks of the metal re-exported, given the incentives of trading houses that profited in energy. The author calls the US stockpile 'US SRB'.
Indian coal imports fell 5.8% y/y in August to 104.6mt, with met coal down 4.18%. Coal India's auction sales premium rose to 140% on low stocks, versus 68% for April-October and 43% for April-July.
Coal India unit South Eastern Coalfields has filed for an India IPO.
The author expects M&A after the correction because commodity supply is very tight. Producers understand supply obstacles better than buyers, governments or fund managers.

Anglo American (AAL.LN): the group CEO was optimistic about diamond sale agreements in principle, with contracts by year end and completion in 2027. Botswana reportedly plans to raise its stake from 18% to 25%, and one bidder, Gareth Penny, reportedly values the stake at $1bn.
Glencore (GLEN.LN): the FT reports on executive pay adjustments, including deferred share award vesting, if a takeover occurs.

Northern Star (NST.AU): the Hemi gold project has a published federal EPBC approval with conditions. WA state approvals and secondary licenses are outstanding, the build is about 2.5 years, and first gold is expected in FY30 at the earliest on a standalone basis.
BP closed the sale of a 65% stake in Castrol to Stonepeak for $6bn, with proceeds to pay down debt. The author says this is not new news.

Gold: speculative selling ran for a fifth straight week. Managed Money, Other and Non-Reportable sold $8bn over Oct 20-27, bringing the cumulative total since Sept 22 to $19.5bn. Gold lost 4.3% from Oct 27-30 as Brent rose 3.7%. Options surface changes showed hedging or outright downside positioning.

China market wrap: A-shares rallied on expectations of more policy support. STAR50, ChiNext and CSI300 ETF volumes surged and growth outperformed high-dividend SOEs. Media rose 7.58% on AI short-video. Gold and coal names traded lower with spot gold.

sector_views.rationale: Supply is impaired by Cochilco's forecast cuts, falling Chilean output and mine accidents, with a record China onshore premium. This is the author's framing and not a formal rating.
The author says resource equities struggle until China participates, but notes policy-support hopes in the China wrap.

earnings_insights: Dongshan Precision rose after a Q3 earnings beat, described as one of the few major Hard Tech names with solid Q3 numbers.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Output and new orders contracted. Non-ferrous metal smelting and rolling and non-metallic minerals softened, and the new export orders sub-index fell to 48.7 from 50.0.
The print missed both the consensus and the desk's estimate.
Falling output from the largest producer supports the supply-impairment argument.

macro_indicators.reading: 330kt in 2026 and 470kt in 2027, about 800kt in total
macro_indicators.interpretation: A tighter supply outlook for copper, in line with the record onshore China premium.
Lower imports alongside a jump in Coal India's auction premium point to tight domestic stocks.

risk_factors: China demand weakness, with the PMI contracting and resource equities dependent on China participation.
Oil headline volatility from supply risk and diplomacy.
Copper tariff and US stockpile re-export policy after the midterms.
Block-cave mine accidents and operational difficulty at El Teniente, Grasberg and Oyu Tolgoi.
Continued speculative gold liquidation and new shorts.
vol_and_positioning: Gold speculative flows: five straight weeks of selling, $8bn sold in the week to Oct 27 and $19.5bn cumulative since Sept 22, split between liquidation ($5.2bn) and new shorts ($2.8bn).
Changes in the gold option surface displayed hedging and/or outright downside implementation.
GS PB reported that all strategies lost money last week.
geopolitical: Oil headlines are swinging between supply risk and diplomacy, with oil moving from $118 to $109 overnight.
US midterm elections are cited as the weekend event behind the October risk-off, and copper tariffs are seen by many traders as a post-midterms event.
The report cites a possible Botswana move to raise its Anglo American diamond stake to 25% from 18%.
